prerequisites: Some familiarity with algorithms and data structures.
Basic notions of complexity are desirable, but not necessary.

learning_outcomes.text: Have deep knowledge and understanding of a limited amount of basic artificial intelligence techniques, including: basic search techniques, heuristic search techniques, optimal-path search techniques, optimal-path search techniques with limited memory usage, game-search techniques, version space machine learning and data mining, backtracking-based constraint techniques, consistency-based constraint techniques, hybrid constraint techniques, Bayesian networks, Markov decision problems, elements of machine learning and neural networks, and general resolution theorem provers for first-order predicate logic.
Be able to simulate each of the above techniques with pen and paper on small examples.
Understand the relevance of these techniques for applications.
Be able to work out solutions on a computer for slightly less small examples using provided didactic tools.
Understand the relationships that exist between these techniques.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: definition and positioning of the course

State representation and search methods: state space representation: positioning and trade-offs, blind search, heuristic search, optimal search, including the A*-algorithm, advanced aspects of heuristic search, heuristic search in game situations
A basis for Machine Learning and Data Mining: Version Spaces as an illustration of Machine Learning, Version Spaces for finding frequent patterns in data (as an illustration of data mining)
Constraint processing: backtracking, backtracking variants, intelligent backtracking, arc consistency techniques, hybrid propagation methods, positioning of applications
Automatic reasoning: introduction, repetition of basic concepts from logic, problem statement and decidability, normalization, unification and resolution in first-order logic

Bayesian Networks: joint probability distribution, conditional independence, representation and semantics of Bayesian networks, modeling with Bayesian networks, deriving conditional independencies from Bayesian networks, principles of inference with Bayesian networks
Markov Decision Processes for probabilistic planning: representation and meaning, inference in Markov decision processes to determine the correct actions and policies
Machine learning: Naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbor, Introduction to neural networks and backpropagation
Solvers in AI: Solvers for SAT and for variants such as model counting (#SAT), Use in logical inference and Bayesian networks, among others
Ethical questions and answers: regarding the implications of AI
Exercises on all content components of the lecture except the introduction.
assessment_rules: The assessment is a written exam during the examination period. The exam consists of multiple-choice questions and open questions. No books are allowed during the exam, but a formula sheet is permitted. The resit modality is the same as the first examination opportunity.
